summary: A dismissal of criminal charges was filed on Thursday, Oct. 8 in 4FA-26-00112CR, the indicted Fairbanks first-degree murder case, three days after a competency stay on it was lifted; the court's public file does not state who filed it, what it reaches or whether the case is at an end, the murder count is still printed with its indicted charge, and no event now stands on the file. A Fourth Judicial District grand jury returned in three cases the same day: a Class B felony count of second-degree assault in a Fairbanks domestic violence case, and six Class A felony methamphetamine counts across two files, one of them against a man the Fairbanks court has had a warrant out for since Sep. 29 with no arrest recorded. The court file in the Oct. 2 sexual abuse conviction now carries the verdicts document, an order of commitment and a March 18, 2027 sentencing date, where on Oct. 8 it carried none of them; that is corrected below. Nine criminal cases were filed in the area on Oct. 8, two of them at Nenana. The filings counts below are the court report's own counts for the week ending Oct. 8. The court opened at least one case that week which that report does not carry: a Minor Offense case filed on Oct. 8, 4FA-26-05258MO, is in a series the criminal charges report does not carry at all.

entries.title: Dismissal of criminal charges filed in a Fairbanks first-degree murder case
body: A docket row dated Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026 in 4FA-26-00112CR, State of Alaska vs. Davenport, Brian Jeffery, reads Dismissal of Criminal Charges. It is the only row of that date and the only row on the file after Oct. 5.

The file carries one count of murder in the first degree, intent to cause death, AS 11.41.100(a)(1)(A), an unclassified felony, offence-dated Jan. 20, 2026 at Fairbanks and recorded as domestic violence related. A grand jury indicted that count on Jan. 29, 2026. The case was filed Jan. 21, 2026 before Judge Temple.

The row immediately above it, dated Oct. 5, is the findings and order on competence for criminal proceedings, commitment and transport, entered with a competency hearing that afternoon. The court's event list records that hearing as an order on competence lifting the stay on the case.

The court's public file does not state who filed the dismissal, which count it reaches, on what basis, or whether the case is at an end. The count is still printed with its indicted charge, no amended charge appears, no disposition code appears, the case status still reads Reopened, and no event of any kind now stands on the event list.
He was charged, not convicted; no conviction was entered on this file. Nothing in the court record describes the offence.

entries.title: Grand jury indicts a second-degree assault count in a Fairbanks domestic violence case
body: A Fourth Judicial District grand jury returned an indictment on Thursday, Oct. 8 in 4FA-26-01946CR, State of Alaska vs. Burdo Jr, William Roger.

The file carries six counts, all at Fairbanks and all recorded as domestic violence related: assault in the second degree, injury with a weapon with intent, AS 11.41.210(a)(1), a Class B felony, offence-dated Sep. 26; assault in the third degree, cause fear of injury with a weapon, AS 11.41.220(a)(1)(A), a Class C felony, offence-dated Sep. 27; two counts of assault in the fourth degree, recklessly injure, Class A misdemeanours; and two counts of criminal mischief in the fifth degree, tamper with property, Class B misdemeanours.

An indicted charge is now carried on the Class B felony and the Class C felony counts. The docket records a grand jury exhibit list, the indictment filed in Superior Court with jurisdiction transferred, a court notice of Superior Court arraignment, the indictment filed in open court, a felony pre-trial order effective Oct. 14, and an indictment or information adding misdemeanour counts to the indictment. A preliminary hearing held Oct. 8 at 3:15 p.m. in Courtroom 102 is recorded as held.

A Superior Court arraignment is set for Oct. 14 at 1:30 p.m. in Courtroom 402 before Judge Bennett, an omnibus hearing for Nov. 3 and a trial week for Nov. 16. He is charged, not convicted. Nothing in the court record describes the incidents or identifies anyone recorded as a victim.

entries.title: Six Class A felony methamphetamine counts indicted in two Fairbanks cases on the same day
body: The same grand jury returned indictments on Thursday, Oct. 8 in two further Fairbanks cases, each carrying three Class A felony counts.

4FA-26-01996CR, State of Alaska vs. Cosca, Anthony Alan, carries three counts offence-dated Mar. 18, Apr. 15 and Jul. 15, 2026 at Fairbanks. All three now carry an indicted charge of misconduct involving a controlled substance in the second degree, manufacture or deliver methamphetamine, AS 11.71.021(a)(2)(A), a Class A felony, alongside an amended charge under the same subsection entered on the day the case was filed. Preliminary hearings stand for Oct. 12 and Oct. 22.

4FA-26-01949CR, State of Alaska vs. Gayvoronskiy, Vitaliy P, carries three counts offence-dated Apr. 27, Aug. 12 and Aug. 27, 2026 at Fairbanks, all three now carrying an indicted charge under the same subsection, stage-dated Oct. 8. No attorney is entered for the defendant, no event of any kind is calendared, and the last process on the file is a warrant issued by the Fairbanks court on Sep. 29 at $10,000 cash performance. The court record does not state that an arrest has been made.

A third Fairbanks case, 4FA-26-01818CR, carries the same three Class A felony counts and was indicted on Sep. 24. The records do not state a connection between any of the three cases. All three defendants are charged, not convicted.

entries.title: The verdicts, an order of commitment and a sentencing date are now on the court file in a Fairbanks sexual abuse case
body: The court file in 4FA-24-02136CR, State of Alaska vs. Dittman, Donald D, now carries a docket row dated Oct. 2, 2026 reading Jury Related Document: Verdicts I and II, a temporary order of commitment pending final judgment of the same date, and a sentencing hearing on Mar. 18, 2027 at 2:30 p.m. in Courtroom 401 on its event list.

Ten docket rows are new since the Oct. 8 reading and all ten carry dates between Sep. 28 and Oct. 2: log notes for five days of jury trial, an order denying a motion on the record, a State's exhibit list, a witness list, a defence exhibit list, a confidential selection of jurors, a note from the jury, the order of commitment and the verdicts document.

The file carries two counts of sexual abuse of a minor in the second degree, contact, AS 11.41.436(a)(3), Class B felonies, both offence-dated Jun. 20, 2024 at Fairbanks and both recorded as domestic violence related. Both were indicted in December 2024. The counts are unchanged and no disposition code appears against either.

The two counts of conviction are known from an Alaska Department of Law release dated Oct. 5, which states that a Fairbanks jury found him guilty on Oct. 2. The sentencing date on the court's event list is the date and time that release gives. The person who was abused is not named in any source carried here.
The Oct. 8 edition's statement that the court file recorded no verdict and no sentencing hearing is corrected below.

body: 4FA-26-02038CR, Aceves, Teddy Bernhard, carries three counts, all offence-dated Oct. 7 at Fairbanks and all recorded as domestic violence related: assault in the fourth degree, recklessly injure, AS 11.41.230(a)(1), and two counts of assault when a child is present, AS 11.41.240(a), all Class A misdemeanours. 4FA-26-02035CR, James, Ryan Bud, carries one count recorded as charging document pending or not filed, with no degree of offence, offence-dated Oct. 8 at Fairbanks, and no docket rows at all. An arraignment is set for Oct. 13. No charge class is stated because none is on the file.

4NE-26-00101CR, Moses, Russell Louis Newman, was filed at the Nenana court and carries four counts, all offence-dated Oct. 4 at Tanana and all recorded as domestic violence related: two counts of assault in the fourth degree, recklessly injure, and two counts of assault when a child is present, all Class A misdemeanours. An arraignment was held Oct. 8 at the Fairbanks courthouse and counsel was appointed from the bench; a rural calendar call is set for Nov. 17 at Nenana. 4FA-26-02029CR, filed Oct. 7 under the same name, now carries one count of indecent exposure in the second degree, AS 11.41.460, a Class B misdemeanour, offence-dated Oct. 6 at Fairbanks. A charging document was filed on Oct. 8 along with a notice of redacting the charging document. An arraignment stands for Oct. 13, with a pre-trial conference Nov. 24 and a trial week Dec. 7.

The count as filed is the subsection for a victim aged 18 or over. The police record of the arrest behind that file, at the 1600 block of East Cowles Street at 21:40 on Oct. 6, carried the label for a victim aged 16 or over. The court file governs the charge.

No charge class was stated for either file until the charging documents were filed. He is charged, not convicted. This is a different person from Cedar Mae Sarten, whose 2024 case is also carried here.

entries.title: Troopers record a concealed loaded pistol at a Van Horn Road traffic stop; the only court file is a non-criminal licence infraction
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch for Oct. 8, incident AK26100321, states that at approximately 00:41 that morning a trooper stopped a Ford SUV after the driver failed to signal while leaving a Van Horn Road bar car park; that the driver, identified as Michael Lamoreaux, was found to be operating without a valid Alaska driver's licence and was asked to step out for field sobriety testing; that while exiting the vehicle he disclosed a concealed pistol in his waistband, which was recovered and found to be loaded; and that he was charged with misconduct involving a weapon in the fifth degree for failing to notify the trooper immediately of the concealed firearm. The entry was posted at 04:50 on Oct. 8.

One court record returns under that name: 4FA-26-05258MO, filed Oct. 8, case type Minor Offense, carrying one count of driving without a valid operator's licence, AS 28.15.011(b), recorded as a non-criminal infraction, offence-dated Oct. 8, on a citation issued by the Alaska State Troopers. The docket records the citation filed, a standing default-judgment notice and a court appearance. An arraignment is set for Oct. 29 at 8:30 a.m.

No count of misconduct involving a weapon appears on that file or on any other court file found under that name, and no criminal case number returns for it. No charge class is stated for the weapons allegation because no charging document carrying it has been found.
The Minor Offense series carries the suffix MO rather than CR and is not carried in the court's weekly criminal charges report. He was charged by the arresting agency, not convicted.

entries.title: Man charged with fourth-degree criminal mischief after damage in the Fairbanks trooper post lobby
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26100318, states that at approximately 23:47 on Oct. 7 troopers responded to the Fairbanks Trooper Post after a man caused damage in the front lobby vestibule and left the area; that he was located about half a mile from the post and identified as Ryan Bud James; that he acted aggressively toward the responding trooper and made threatening statements; that he was detained without further incident and admitted tampering with fire alarm equipment at the post, which had triggered an audible alarm; and that he was charged with criminal mischief in the fourth degree for damaging and tampering with fire protection equipment in a public building. The entry was posted at 05:59 on Oct. 8.

No court file carrying that count has been identified. One case number was opened under that name on Oct. 8, 4FA-26-02035CR, and it records one count as charging document pending or not filed. A separate police record states that a man of that name was arrested at the 1600 block of East Cowles Street at 01:46 on Oct. 8 on a charge of criminal trespass in the second degree. No court file carrying that count has been identified either.
He was charged by the arresting agency, not convicted, and no charge class is stated. The records do not state a connection between the events.

entries.title: A Sep. 7 trooper arrest of two people was published on Oct. 8, thirty-one days later
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26100024, states that on Sep. 7, 2026 the troopers' Fairbanks-based Criminal Suppression Unit arrested Brianna Perry and William Clatterbuck for unlawful contact and violation of conditions of release. The entry was posted on Oct. 8, thirty-one days after the date it describes, and gives no time, no location beyond Fairbanks and no further detail.

Two court files were opened on Oct. 8, 4FA-26-02039CR and 4FA-26-02040CR, each carrying three counts of unlawful contact per court order and one count of violating a condition of release for a felony, all Class A misdemeanours and all offence-dated Sep. 9, 2026 at Fairbanks.
The dispatch gives the arrest date as Sep. 7 and both court files give the offence date as Sep. 9. Both are arrested and charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Troopers record two death investigations at Fairbanks on Oct. 8, neither of them criminal
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26100584, states that on Oct. 8 troopers responded to a residence on Chena Hot Springs Road to investigate a death and found that Margaret Qualley had passed away from natural causes, and that next of kin have been notified. The entry was posted at 22:48 on Oct. 8.

A second entry, incident AK26100497, states that at approximately 12:34 on Oct. 8 troopers in Fairbanks received a report of a welfare check, that the person being checked on was found deceased at their residence, that no criminal aspect is suspected and that next of kin has been notified. That entry names no one. It was posted at 15:51 on Oct. 8.
No crime is alleged in either. No finding has been announced by the State Medical Examiner's Office on either death. The dispatch states a manner of death in the first and states none in the second.

entries.title: Man arrested at Tok and remanded to the Fairbanks jail, held without bail
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26100452, states that on Oct. 8 troopers in Tok received a report of an assault and that the investigation resulted in the arrest of Thomias Smith, 27, of Tok, for sexual assault in the second degree, assault in the second degree, assault in the third degree and criminal mischief in the fifth degree, and that he was remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center and held without bail.

Tok is outside the Fairbanks area; the arrest is carried because of the remand to the Fairbanks jail. No court file returns under that name on a dated name search, and no charge class is stated. He was arrested, not convicted. Nothing in the record identifies anyone recorded as a victim.

Preliminary hearings were held on Oct. 8 at 3:15 p.m. in Courtroom 102 in 4FA-26-01866CR, Burton, Jerald, and in 4NE-26-00097CR, Chambers, Jennifer Sara, the second five days after that case was indicted and transferred to Superior Court. The charges on both files are unchanged.

Private counsel entered on Oct. 8 in 4FA-26-02010CR, Gonzalez-Mellado, Manuel, and in 4FA-26-02031CR, Morry, Miranda A. A summons was issued in 4FA-26-02034CR, Griswold, Arthur Ervin, and a return of service was filed in 4FA-26-01997CR, Sam, Elijay John. All of these defendants are charged, not convicted.
